beats: [d:intrigue][sfx:boom][act:setting the scene, a sense of scale]A giant ^snake made of earth, four hundred metres long, ^uncoils along a ridge in Ohio, in the United States.
[d:tension][act:the hook, wonder in the voice]And on the longest day of the year, its head seems to ^swallow the setting ^sun.

[d:calm][act:describing it, unhurried]Picture a bank of earth about as wide as a ^road, and about ^waist high. [act:describing it, one by one]A coiled ^tail, a winding body, open ^jaws, and an ^oval in its mouth. [p:0.93][act:a sense of scale]End to end along its curves, about four football ^pitches. [go:2|0][act:showing you, gently]Now sight along the ^head, and it points to where the sun sets on the ^longest day: the summer ^solstice.

[d:build][act:presenting the claim, fair and even]The writer Graham Hancock suggests the layout could be far older than its builders: about ^thirteen thousand years, back in the ^Ice Age. [p:0.93][act:explaining his logic, fair]His clue is Earth's ^tilt. [act:explaining, clear]Our planet spins on a leaning axis, and that lean very slowly ^rocks, over tens of thousands of years. [act:explaining, clear]As it rocks, the solstice sunset creeps along the ^horizon. [act:the claim at its strongest]So, the argument goes, the exact point the head aims at could tell you the ^year it was aimed.
[d:build][act:lighter, a curious aside]And some see the constellation ^Draco, the dragon, a winding line of stars, in its coils.

[d:build][act:laying out the evidence, precise]So what do the ^dates say? [p:0.93][act:explaining, clear]Charcoal holds a natural clock, radioactive carbon that fades at a steady pace, like a candle burning ^down. [act:explaining, clear]And anything ^beneath a mound was there first, like a coin under a ^carpet. [act:laying out the evidence, precise]Samples from inside and beneath the mound split archaeologists into two camps: the ^Adena people, about {300|^three hundred} BCE, or the Fort ^Ancient people, about {1070|^ten seventy} CE.
[d:build][sfx:shimmer][act:the point, quietly firm]^Both inside the last ^three thousand years. [act:plain, gentle]And nothing at the site dates to the ^Ice Age.

[d:reveal][sfx:hit][act:turning to it, one eyebrow up][tune:rise]And the ^tilt argument? [act:plain fact, measured]Over thirteen thousand years, the solstice sunset moves by ^less than a degree. [p:0.93][act:the everyday picture]That's less than the width of your little finger, held at arm's ^length. [act:the sting, dry and gentle]Smaller than the ^error in sighting along a ^rebuilt head of earth, several metres wide.
[d:aside][act:a light aside, matter of fact]And the dragon of Draco is a picture drawn by peoples of the ^Mediterranean, an ocean ^away.

[d:verdict][p:0.95][act:weighing it, calm authority][tune:rise]An ^Ice Age serpent? [act:the verdict, firm and kind][tune:fall]*Ruled ^out*. [act:brighter, genuinely curious][tune:fall]^Adena or Fort ^Ancient builders? [act:warm, inviting]That's the ^real open question.
[d:tension][p:0.93][act:the last word, warm and proud]Either way, it's ^Native American ^genius, aimed at the sun.
